basis: Defective renal tubular urate reabsorption causes hypouricemia and hyperuricosuria; renal injury remains within the renal axis.
Defining skeletal growth abnormalities, patellar hypoplasia and microtia; feeding difficulties and microcephaly alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Renal salt-wasting tubulopathy with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis; nephrocalcinosis in 7/8 remains within the renal axis.
Defined as familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; DMD causation and unspecified muscle histology do not establish common skeletal muscle disease.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and structural brain abnormalities; fixed flexion contractures in 2/6 (~33%) support musculoskeletal involvement.
Disease of central or peripheral autonomic nerves; no additional directly damaged organ applies across this umbrella.
Defining hypotrichosis, lymphatic vascular malformation with lymphedema, and telangiectasia; thin skin occurs in 2/4.
Gambiense trypanosomiasis commonly progresses to CNS invasion and meningoencephalitis (>30% over untreated course); skin findings do not establish common lasting damage.
Progressive heterotopic ossification; conductive hearing loss and alopecia each occur in 30-79%. Respiratory restriction reflects chest-wall disease, not direct lung damage.
Benign tumor arising in the breast, which has no axis.
Congenital cleft lip with or without cleft palate directly affects oral anatomy.
Defining hair/skin pigmentation abnormalities and sensorineural hearing loss (12/14); iris pigmentation changes alone do not impair ocular function.
Obstruction of urinary outflow; the entire urinary tract belongs to the renal axis.
Benign urothelial neoplasm arising in the renal pelvis.
Inherited amyloid protein deposition with predominant nephropathy; GI involvement annotated 30-79%; hepatic dysfunction, neuropathy and heart failure are 5-29%.
Usually a subcutaneous myopericyte neoplasm; perivascular growth does not imply vascular dysfunction. EBV association is not defining across most cases.
Defined by severe proportionate short stature and hip dislocation; no other organ involvement is established.
Split spinal cord with myelomeningocele through a congenital vertebral closure defect; no additional common direct organ damage is established.
Defining limb and skeletal malformations; hearing, renal, ocular and neurodevelopmental findings have unspecified frequencies and cannot establish the 30% threshold.
Rubella virus infection; the brief rash is transient. Congenital organ damage belongs to the congenital rubella subtype, not most patients across rubella.
Defined bilirubin metabolism disorder; elevated circulating bilirubin alone does not establish hepatic injury, blood-cell disease or neurologic damage.
Infection located in the urinary tract, which belongs to the renal axis.
Cutaneous ectoparasitic infestation by mites, including scabies and trombiculiasis.
Defined developmental eye disorder caused by defective PAX6 regulation; additional organ disease is not established.
Neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic-pituitary disorder with hypogonadism and growth hormone dysfunction; hypotonia and feeding symptoms do not establish separate tissue damage.
